entries.title: Hosea 12:2 "dispute"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:2 "dispute" The term "dispute" (BDB 936) means a legal lawsuit (cf. Hosea 2:2; 4:14; Deut. 25:1; 2 Sam. 15:2,4; Micah 6:2; 7:9). Judah and Jacob (i.e. Israel) are both guilty (cf. Hosea 4:9b).

▣ "He will repay him according to his ways" Be not deceived, God is not mocked; for whatsoever a man sows, that shall he reap (cf. Job 34:11,25; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 12:14; 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Ezek. 33:20; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12). Notice this "reaping and sowing" is also seen in Hosea 8:7; 10:12-13.

entries.title: Hosea 12:3-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:3-4 This is a play on the names Jacob and Israel. "Jacob" is defined in Gen. 25:26 as, "one who took his brother by the heel." The term can also mean "supplanter," "usurper," or "deceiver" (BDB 784). The term "Israel" is defined in Gen. 32:28 as "one who contends with God."

Bethel was once a special holy site where Jacob (Israel) met YHWH. Now Israel had turned it into an especially evil, idolatrous location.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "he contended with God. . .he wrestled with an angel" These are parallel. The Angel of the Lord is in view as a personal, physical representative of God Himself (cf. Gen. 16:7-13; 22:11-15; 24:7,40; 31:11,13; 48:15-16; Exod. 3:2,4; 13:21; 14:19; Jdg. 2:1; 6:22-23; 13:3-32; Zech. 3:1-2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE LORD

12:4
NASB  "He spoke with us"
NKJV  "He spoke to us"
NJB  "God spoke to us"
NRSV, REB, TEV, Peshitta, NET  "he spoke with him"
LXX  "and intreated me"

The MT has "us," but the context demands "him." The UBS Text Project, p. 262, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

  1. "with us" ‒ עמנו
  2. "with him" ‒ עמו

entries.title: Hosea 12:5 "the God of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:5 "the God of hosts" This verse has three names for the God of Israel who appeared to Jacob at the river (i.e. Gen. 32).

  1. YHWH
  2. Eloah of Hosts
  3. YHWH His memorial

  This is a reference to the God of Hosts, which means

  1. the "captain of the armies in heaven"
  2. the "head of the heavenly council" (BDB 838, e.g. 2 Sam. 5:10)
  3. in Babylonian astral worship context it can refer to the stars of heaven, which they saw as supernatural beings who influenced their lives

This is the most common title for Godin the post-exilic books (cf. Amos 3:13; 6:14; and 9:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

▣ "The Lord is His name" This is literally "His memorial" (BDB 271). Names reveal and reflect character traits (e.g. Ps. 135:13). This refers to the name YHWH, which was revealed to Moses in Exod. 3:14. Before this time the patriarchs addressed God as El Shaddai (cf. Exod. 6:2-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

entries.title: Hosea 12:6 "Return to your God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:6 "Return to your God" Here is the call to repentance again ("return," BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERFECT, but functioning as a JUSSIVE). And again these special terms reappear (cf. Hosea 2:19; 4:1; 6:6; 10:12; Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8). Knowing God must result in lifestyle change that reflects His character!

In many ways, this verse is a summary of the book of Hosea.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "Observe. . .wait" These are both IMPERATIVES:

  1. observe, BDB 1036, KB 1501, Qal IMPERATIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  2. wait, BDB 875, KB 1082, Piel IMPERATIVE (i.e. demonstrate life long trust, cf. Lam. 3:25; Micah 7:7).

▣ "kindness" This is the important covenant term hesed (BDB 338 I).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "justice" See SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

entries.title: Hosea 12:7 "A merchant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:7 "A merchant" This is a word play on "Canaanite" (BDB 488 II, cf. Isa. 23:8; Ezek. 16:29; 17:4). This seems to be sarcasm! The term can mean either an ethnic group or a merchant. Israel was acting like the Canaanites (i.e. "false balances," cf. Prov. 11:1; 20:23; Amos 8:5). These greedy merchants are possibly referred to in Hosea 7:14c.

▣ "He loves to oppress" This VERB (BDB 798, KB 897, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is used in Deut. 24:14. Oppression of the poor is not allowed among YHWH's people (cf. Prov. 14:31; 22:16; Amos 4:1; Jer. 7:6; Ezek. 22:29; Zech. 7:10). This is the opposite of Hosea 12:6! This word is often used in a negative sense of Israel loving the wrong things (cf. Hosea 4:17-18; 10:11; 12:7; Amos 4:4-5; Micah 3:1-2).

entries.title: Hosea 12:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:8 Israel thought her dishonestly gained wealth was a sign of covenant blessings (i.e. Lev. 26; Deut. 28), but it was the opposite!

▣
NASB  "no iniquity, which would be sin"
NKJV  "They shall find in me no iniquity that is sin"
NRSV  "No offense has been found in me that would be sin"
TEV  "And no one can accuse us of getting rich dishonestly"
NJB  "But of all his gains he will keep nothing because of the
  sin of which he is guilty"
NET  "In all I have done to gain wealth, no one can accuse
  me of any offense that is actually sinful
REB  "but despite all my gains the guilt of sin will not
  be found in me"
Peshitta  "all my labors will not be enough to rid me of the sin
  which I have sinned"
JPSOA  "All my gains do not amount to an offense which
  is real guilt"

The Septuagint retranslates this following some Hebrew MSS, "None of his labors shall be found available to him by reason of the sins which he has committed," which seems to be the indictment of the prophet or court prosecutor.

If the MT, reflected in the NASB, is retained, Israel (i.e. Ephraim) is asserting she will never bear this guilt.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

entries.title: Hosea 12:9 "I have been the Lord your God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:9 "I have been the Lord your God" This is the full covenant title of Israel's God (cf. Hosea 12:5; Exod. 20:2).

▣ "I will make you live in tents again,

  As in the days of the appointed festival" This can refer to two opposite interpretations:

  1. the wilderness time was seen as the ideal time (rabbis say "a honeymoon period") between YHWH and His covenant people (cf. Hosea 2:14; 9:10; 11:1-4; Jer. 2:2; Amos 2:10)
  2. in a negative sense as the Israelites lived in the make-shift houses during the Feast of Booths (cf. Lev. 23:42-44), YHWH will, in His judgment, make them live in make-shift houses on a permanent basis (opposite of Hosea 8:14)

The immediate context (i.e. Hosea 12:8) demands option #2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I. D. #3

entries.title: Hosea 12:10 "I have also spoken"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:10 "I have also spoken" This verse asserts that YHWH has adequately revealed Himself and His will to Israel through the prophets (cf. Hosea 6:5). He did this in visions and parables. He earlier had revealed Himself through His laws (i.e. the writings of Moses, cf. Hosea 4:6; 8:1,11).

The prophets were covenant mediators. They did not bring additional requirements, but turned people's thoughts back to their commitments to the ancient covenants (i.e. Abraham, the Patriarchs, Moses, David). They check the motives as well as the performance of these covenant stipulations. They draw out the current application and significance of the ancient God-given ways.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

▣
NASB, NJB, JPSOA  "parables"
NKJV  "symbols"
NRSV  "destruction"
TEV  "warnings"
Peshitta  "similitudes"

This is probably the OT background for Jesus' use of parables. The VERB (BDB 197 I, KB 225, Piel IMPERFECT) means "to be like" (i.e. parable on similitude). The context and emphasis is on YHWH's active revelation in the life of Israel, but they would not listen (cf. Isa. 6:9-13). Parables both enlighten the believing and confuse the unbelieving (cf. Mark 4:10-12).

Some scholars think the Hebrew means "oracle of doom" (BDB 198 II, cf. Hosea 4:5,6; 10:7,15[twice]; NRSV, TEV).

  1. used parables ‒ אדמה
  2. used oracle of doom (lit. "cause to cease") ‒ דמה

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES

12:11
NASB, NRSV, NJB  "iniquity"
NKJV, TEV  "idols"
REB  "idolatry"
JPSOA  "worthless"
LXX  "nothing"

This is the term awen (BDB 19), which can mean "trouble," "sorrow," "wickedness," or "idolatry" (i.e. Bethel called Aven in Hosea 4:15; 5:8; 10:5). The parallel in the next line, "worthless" (BDB 996), implies that both refer to idolatry (Canaanite fertility worship). The "House of God" has become the house of wickedness!!

SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

▣ "Gilead" Also see Hosea 6:8-9.

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV  "sacrifice bulls"
NJB  "sacrifice to bulls"
REB  "sacrificed to bull-gods"
JPSOA  "sacrificing oxen"
Peshitta  "sacrificed bullocks"

A better understanding may be "to bulls" (i.e. the golden calf replicas) which had become Ba'al idols.

▣ "Gilgal. . .the heap of stones" This (BDB 164) is a play on the term "Gilgal," which means "circle of stones" (BDB 166). For that matter there may be an intentional word play between "Gilead," "Gilgal," and "stone heaps." Because of Israel's rebellion, this sacred site will be turned from a memorial to YHWH into a heap of stones (i.e. pieces of the Ba'al pillars) and a plowed field!

This Gilgal seems to be located in the north of Israel, south of Dor, near the coast (cf. Josh. 12:23; see IVP Bible Background Commentary [OT], p. 330).

Here is the problem.

  1. Gilgal is a common name for cultic locations.
  2. In Amos 4:4; 5:5, it is related to Bethel, therefore, near Jericho (Josh. 4).
  3. In Hosea 9:15; 12:11, it is related to a northern coastal city south of Dor (cf. Josh. 12:23).

Even if the exact location is in doubt, the site is related to pagan worship.

Young's Concordance to the Bible, p. 391, lists four different Gilgals.

entries.title: Hosea 12:12 "Now Jacob"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:12 "Now Jacob" This seems to refer to Hosea 12:4-6, which relates to the historical life of Jacob (i.e. Israel, cf. Gen. 28-30).

entries.title: Hosea 12:13 "by a prophet the Lord brought Israel from Egypt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:13 "by a prophet the Lord brought Israel from Egypt" This must refer to Moses as a prophet (cf. Deut. 18:15; 34:10). The very event of YHWH using Moses to bring Israel out of Egypt is Exod. 14:19-22; Isa. 63:11-14.

entries.title: Hosea 12:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:14 The nation of Israel is not acting like Israel, but like Jacob and will bear her own sin. The blood guilt may refer to murder or child sacrifice (i.e. to Molech).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

▣ "Lord" This is the title Adon.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

entries.title: Hosea 13:1 "When Ephraim spoke there was trembling"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:1 "When Ephraim spoke there was trembling" There are two possible understandings of this verse. This is an unusual use of the term "Ephraim" because it seems not to be a reference to the entire Northern Ten Tribes, but to the arrogance ("He exalted himself," BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PERFECT) of that individual tribe only (e.g. Jdg. 8:1; 12:1). The fear of this tribe can be seen in that when it spoke, the other tribes "trembled" (BDB 958). Remember that Ephraim and Manasseh are half-tribes because they are the children of Joseph (cf. Gen. 48), but they represent the largest tribe, both geographically and numerically.

The second possibility is that Ephraim stands for the leaders and king of the capital, Samaria. It was the first king (i.e. Jeroboam I) who set up the golden calves as a rival to the Jerusalem temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 16:31). It was Ahab and Jezebel who brought Ba'al worship to Israel (cf. 1 Kgs. 16:31).

The third option

  1. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, Peshitta ‒ "trembling"
  2. REB ‒ "a prince and leader"
  3. JPSOA ‒ "spoke piety"
  4. LXX ‒ "received statutes"

This NOUN (BDB 958) appears only here in the OT, but it does appear in the DSS as "tremble."

I think what verse 1 means is that when Ephraim spoke with awe (i.e. trembling) of YHWH, they were honored (i.e. lifted up), but when they sinned by being involved in Ba'al worship, they were judged.

▣
NASB, NKJV  "he exalted himself"
NRSV, REB, JPSOA, NET  "he was exalted"
NJB  "he was a power"
LXX  "he adopted ordinances for himself"
Peshitta  "he became great"

The MT has the VERB "lifted" (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PERFECT). The question is

  1. did he exalt himself (MT)
  2. was he exalted by others (JPSOA)

The diference involves only what vowels are added to the older Hebrew text by the Masoretic scholars.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

▣ "Baal" This refers to the male fertility god of the Canaanite pantheon (cf. Hosea 2:8; 9:10). For an excellent reference see William Foxwell Albright's book, Archaeology and the Religion of Israel, page 72ff.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP IN THE ANE

▣ "he did wrong and died" This refers to the powers and preeminence of the tribe ceasing ("died" BDB 559, KB 562, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, used as imagery for YHWH's judgment, e.g. of Moab in Amos 2:2; of Israel in Ezek. 18:31).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Hosea 13:2 "molten images. . .idols"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:2 "molten images. . .idols" This may refer to the golden calves of Bethel and Dan (cf. line 5). However, these descriptions do not exactly fit them. They were made of wood and overlaid with gold. Therefore, this may refer to images at local Ba'al shrines (cf. Hosea 2:8; Isa. 40:19-20; 44:12-17; 46:6-7; Jer. 10:3-5).

▣ "Let the men who sacrifice kiss the calves" We learn from 1 Kgs. 19:18 that kissing the idol's feet (Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 334, thinks they blew kisses at the idol) was part of Ba'al worship (the VERB could be an IMPERFECT or a JUSSIVE, NASB). This is one example of how the supposed worship of YHWH, by means of the golden calves, was corrupted into Ba'al worship. They worshiped what they made but it could not see, hear, or act!

For historical examples of kissing idols' feet, see IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 759.

entries.title: Hosea 13:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:3 There are four elements mentioned which describe Israel in her transitoriness and rebellion (cf. Isa. 44:22; Hos. 6:4), which will be quickly judged and removed: morning cloud, dew, chaff, and smoke.

▣ "chimney" Literally this is "window" (BDB 70). Chimneys were non-existent in the ancient world. The buildings had small windows close to the ceiling for the purpose of letting the smoke out. Many homes placed the fire in the center of the room and allowed the smoke to exit at whatever window was possible.

entries.title: Hosea 13:4 "Yet I have been the Lord your God
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:4 "Yet I have been the Lord your God

 Since the land of Egypt" This is how YHWH introduced His Ten Commandments (cf. Exod. 20:2; Deut. 5:6). This, again, is a reference to the Exodus as the courtship and honeymoon time between YHWH and Israel (cf. Hosea 13:5; 2:14; 9:10; 12:9).

▣ "you were not to know any god except Me" This phrase is in the Ten Commandments (cf. Exod. 20:3; Deut. 5:7). The VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERFECT) implies intimate, personal relationship (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil PARTICIPLE, e.g. Isa. 43:3,11,14; 45:15,21-22; 63:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "For there is no savior besides Me" YHWH was the only One and the only Redeemer (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil PARTICIPLE, e.g. Isa. 43:3,11,14; 45:15,21-22; 63:8; also note Deut. 32:39).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

entries.title: Hosea 13:5 "I cared for you in the wilderness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:5 "I cared for you in the wilderness" The VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT) is literally "to know" (i.e. meaning chosen and given special knowledge of YHWH). God's special care of Israel showed His love (cf. Deut. 32:10-14).

The ancient Greek and Syriac translations have "fed" (BDB 944) instead of "cared."

  1. "I cared (lit. knew) for you" ‒ ידעתיך, MT
  2. "I fed you" ‒ רעיתיך, LXX, Peshitta

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR CARING

▣
NASB, NRSV  "In the land of drought"
NKJV  "in the land of great drought"
TEV  "desert land"
NJB  "in a land of dreadful drought"
REB  "in a land of burning heat"
JPSOA  "in a thirsty land"
LXX  "in an uninhabitable land"

This CONSTRUCT, which is found only here in the OT, means "intense heat and dryness." It is a way of alluding to YHWH's supernatural provision of water during the wilderness wandering period (e.g. Exod. 15:22-26; 17:1-7; Num. 20:2-13; 21:16; Deut. 32:10-14).

entries.title: Hosea 13:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:6 What a tragedy! God's blessings ("satisfied" [twice] BDB 959, KB 1302, the first Qal IMPERFECT and the second Qal PERFECT with waw) turned into self-centered pride and spiritual fatness (cf. Deut. 6:10-12; 8:11-20; 32:13-15).

▣ "Therefore they forgot Me" Here is the tragedy. They took the physical, but missed the truly valuable—a personal relationship with the only Creator, Redeemer God (cf. Hosea 2:13; 4:6; ;8:14; Deut. 8:14; 31:16,20; 32:15,18; Jdg. 10:6).

entries.title: Hosea 13:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:7 It is interesting that the ancient translations (LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate) add, "on the way of Assyria," implying this refers to the Assyrian exile. Assyria is specifically mentioned in Hosea 7:11; 8:9; 9:3; 10:6; 11:11.

entries.title: Hosea 13:7-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:7-8 These are references to wild animals as imagery for YHWH's judgment: lion, leopard, bear, and lioness (e.g. Jer. 2:15; 4:7; 5:5; Ps. 7:2; 50:22). This animal attack contrasts the shepherding imagery of Hosea 13:6.

In Hosea, YHWH being described as a lion or lioness can be both

  1. positive ‒ YHWH as protector, Hosea 11:10-11
  2. negative ‒ YHWH as judge, Hosea 5:14; 13:7-8 (also note Amos 1:2; 3:4,8; 5:19)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Hosea 13:9 "That you are against Me, against your help"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:9 "That you are against Me, against your help" The Hebrew text is ambiguous. The UBS Text Project, pp. 266-267, gives three possibilities.

  1. "that which has caused your destruction, O Israel, is that you are against me (who is your help)"
  2. "that which has cause your destruction, O Israel, is that in me alone is your help (while you looked for it elsewhere)" [JPSOA]
  3. "that which has caused your destruction, O Israel, is that in me, you look for your help (that is, trusting blindly in my longsuffering and patience)"

What an irony! Israel had forsaken her only help (i.e. YHWH, cf., Jer. 2:17,19). The LXX and Peshitta translations have, "For who will help you?"

entries.title: Hosea 13:10 "Where now is your king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:10 "Where now is your king" The MT has "I want to be your king," (or "I will be"), but several ancient translations (LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate) emend the text to read like the NASB.

The MT has "I will be" (אהי, BDB 224, NKJV) but most ancient and modern translations emend it to "where" (איה). The UBS Text Project, p. 267, gives "where" a "B" rating (cf. NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta, Targums, Vulgate).

entries.title: Hosea 13:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:10-11 This seems to be another reference that relates to Hosea's negative attitude toward the monarchy (cf. Hosea 7:3-7; 8:4,10,13; 10:3), but it may also reflect Deuteronomy 28 (esp. Hosea 13:36,52).

  1. The line 11a, "I gave you a king in My anger," reflects 2 Sam. 8:4-9.
  2. The next line, 11b, represents the exile by Assyria (cf. 2 Kgs. 17:1-6).

entries.title: Hosea 13:12 "bound up"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:12 "bound up" The VERB (BDB 864, KB 1058, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) means the retention of guilt.

▣ "His sin is stored up" The VERB (BDB 860, KB 1049, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) is imagery for "remembered" or "cataloged" (cf. Hosea 7:2; 8:13; 9:9). This refers to YHWH's judicial decision of Israel's guilt, written on a legal document.

entries.title: Hosea 13:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:13 This image ("pains of childbirth" BDB 408, KB 411, Qal PARTICIPLE) seems to refer to

  1. Israel as an unborn son who is reluctant to come out of the womb and, therefore, is spiritually dead (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:3; Isa. 37:3)
  2. labor pains as a symbol of judgment (cf. Micah 4:9-10)

Israel should have recognized the pain and repented (cf. Isa. 21:3; 26:17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIRTH PAINS

entries.title: Hosea 13:14 "Shall I ransom. . .Shall I redeem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:14 "Shall I ransom. . .Shall I redeem" The first VERB (BDB 804, KB 911) is a Qal IMPERFECT and second VERB (BDB 145, KB 169) a Qal IMPERFECT. These two parallel phrases can be interpreted as INTERROGATIVES (i.e. "where," see v. 10 notes, questions, cf. NASB; JPSOA) or as INDICATIVES (statements, UBS Text Project, p. 268, gives this a "B" rating, cf. NIV). The Septuagint translates them as INDICATIVES and this is quoted by Paul in 1 Cor. 15:55. However, the Masoretic Text, in context, seems to imply that they are questions (NASB) and they imply judgment (Hosea 13:14e, NET Bible, p. 1577, #13).

This is such a wonderful promise in the midst of a judgment context! There are several OT passages that promise a new day of hope in the face of death (cf. Ps. 73:24; Isa. 25:8; 26:19; Dan. 12:2). Of course, the great passages in the NT are

  1. Paul ‒ 1 Cor. 15
  2. John ‒ Rev. 21-22

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

▣ "the power of Sheol" Notice how this verse personifies death (see note at Rom. 6:23).

  1. "hand" of Sheol (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND)
  2. ransom. . .redeem from
  3. addressed as
    1. O Death
    2. O Sheol

Verses such as these contributed to the concept of a "Grim Reaper," but in the Bible, YHWH is in control of death, as He is resurrection.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEATH ANGEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

▣ "thorns. . .sting" These are images (i.e. "plagues" BDB 184 and "destruction" BDB 881) of the means and fear of death.

▣ "Compassion will be hidden from My sight" The JPSOA has "Revenge shall be far from My thoughts," basing this on the use of "compassion" (BDB 637) in Deut. 32:36; Isa. 1:24. The NRSV and NIV translations group v. 14 with Hosea 13:15-16.

13:15
NASB, JPSOA  "Though he flourishes among the reeds"
NKJV, REB  "Though he is fruitful among his brethren"
NRSV  "Although he may flourish among the rushes"
TEV  "Even though Israel flourishes like weeds"
NJB  "Though Ephraim bears more fruit than his
  brothers"

The MT has "though he a son of brothers may bear fruit." The ancient translations (LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate) have "he causes division between brothers." Modern translations such as the NASB assume an emendation of "reed" for "brother."

  1. among brothers ‒ בין אחים (UBS Text Project gives an "B" rating)
  2. among reeds ‒ בין אחוים (see NET Bible, p. 1578, #1)

The VERB "bear fruit" (BDB 826, KB 903, Hiphil IMPERFECT) is a word play on "Ephraim." However, YHWH's east wind (Assyria) is coming and he will be fruitful no more (i.e. the water will be dried up). War will devastate his people, his most vulnerable ones (cf. Hosea 13:16)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: EAST WIND

▣ "The wind of the Lord" This phrase refers to Assyria as a chosen tool of YHWH for the chastisement of His people, Israel (cf. Hosea 12:1; Isa. 10:5).

▣ "will become dry. . .will be dried up" This parallelism required an emendation.

"Will become dry," line d, is "ashamed" (BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT) in the MT, but the LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate have "will be dry" (BDB 386, KB 384, Hiphil IMPERFECT). This emendation is suggested by the BDB.

  1. MT, "and will be ashamed" ‒ ויבושׁ
  2. LXX, Peshitta "and shall dry up" ‒ ויבושׁ

entries.title: Hosea 13:16 "They will fall by the sword"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:16 "They will fall by the sword" This refers to the collapse of the capital, Samaria, in 722 B.C. by Assyria. This verse vividly describes the horror of ancient warfare (see note at Hosea 10:14). The entire population suffers (cf. Isa. 10:24-27).

entries.title: Hosea 14:1 "Return"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:1 "Return" This (BDB 996, KB 1427) is a Qal IMPERATIVE. "Return" is a recurrent theme in Hosea (e.g. Hosea 3:5; 5:4; 6:1; 7:10,16; 11:5; 12:6; 14:1-2). True repentance brings physical and spiritual benefits! Remember that repentance is related to personal relationship (i.e. "return to the Lord your God," e.g. Hosea 2:13; 4:6; 8:14; 13:6; Amos 4:6,9,10,11) as much as it is to rules!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (NT)

▣ "stumbled" The OT imagery for unstable footing is used to describe the spiritual life. Sure footing is a sign of a healthy spiritual life, while stumbling (BDB 505, KB 502, Qal PERFECT) is a sign of sin (cf. Hosea 5:5b; Isa. 3:8; 59:10,14; Jer. 46:6).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Hosea 14:2 "Take words with you and return to the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:2 "Take words with you and return to the Lord" This sentence (Hosea 14:1 in MT) has four Qal IMPERATIVES and one Piel COHORTATIVE. YHWH demands that Israel respond appropriately!

  1. "take" ‒ BDB 542, KB 534
  2. "return" ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427
  3. "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65
  4. "present" ‒ BDB 1022, KB 1522 (Piel COHORTATIVE)

Notice the repetition of "take." If Israel will truly repent then YHWH will completely accept and restore them!

This refers to the sacrificial system (i.e. MT "our lips as bulls"). To better understand this phrase we should add "take words not lambs." This affirms the proper restoration of Mosaic sacrifice.

The NET Bible, p. 1578, #10, has a good insight into the repeated use of the VERB (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE.

  1. take your confession to YHWH, v. 2a
  2. He will take away all your iniquity

Oh, the power of repentance and Oh, the matchless, unchanging mercy of YHWH!

▣ "Take away all iniquity" The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT) is surrounded by IMPERATIVES. This phrase occurs several times (7) in the OT with YHWH as its subject (cf. Exod. 34:7; Num. 14:18; Ps. 32:5; 85:2; Isa. 33:24; Hosea 14:2; Micah 7:18) and always means "remove iniquity" (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 162). It is a plea from truly repentant covenant people.

▣ "iniquity" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #2.

▣
NASB, NKJV  "And receive us graciously"
NRSV, JPSOA  "accept that which is good"
TEV  "accept our prayers"
NJB, REB  "accept our wealth"
LXX  "you receive good things"
Peshitta  "receive blessings"

What does the Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE (BDB 373 I), used as an ADVERB mean in this context? The root has several usages.

  1. KB 370 I ‒ good, merry, pleasant, desirable
  2. KB 371 II ‒ perfume (i.e. good smelling)
  3. KB 371 III ‒ an Aramean state
  4. KB 371 IV ‒ word, speech, prayer (i.e. related to Qal IMPERATIVE, "take," which is an IMPERATIVE OF REQUEST
  5. KB 373 ‒ good things, prosperity, blessings, well-being

Number 4's connotation is is found only here, but seems to fit the context best.

▣
NASB  "That we may present the fruit of our lips"
NKJV  "For we will offer the sacrifices of our lips"
NKJV (footnote)  "For we will offer the bull calves of our lips"
NRSV  "and we will offer the fruit of our lips"
TEV  "and we will praise you as we have promised"
Peshitta  "then he will recompense you for the prayer
  of your lips"
NJB  "instead of bulls we will dedicate to you our
  lips"
REB  "we shall pay our vows with cattle from our
  pens"
NET Bible  "that we may offer the praise of our lips as
  sacrificial bulls"

The VERB (BDB 1022, KB 1532, Piel COHORTATIVE) basically means "to complete," here to pay a vow (e.g. 2 Sam. 15:7; Ps. 50:14; 66:13; 116:14,18; Isa. 19:21). This refers to confession, prayer, and praise (cf. Heb. 13:15). This passage is used by modern Judaism to rationalize the place of prayer as a substitute for sacrifice (cf. Ps. 50; 69:30-31). Mosaic Judaism ceased with the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in A.D. 70, by the Roman army under Titus. Mosaic Judaism requires a temple and priests! Modern Judaism is not Mosaic; it is Talmudic and rabbinical. I have come to believe that

  1. Jesus' words in Matt. 23; 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21
  2. Paul's words in 2 Thess. 2
  3. John's words in the book of Revelation

all refer to the 1st century history. Please look at my new notes (2024) on these texts free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org.

The above translation and interpretation, so popular among Jewish sources, reflects the Septuagint. The MT reads, "as bulls our lips" (UBS Text Project, pp. 269-270, gives the MT a "B" rating). The Hebrew is uncertain and the context must fill in the necessary gaps! In context this would refer to

  1. prayer (LXX)
  2. worship of bull calves (MT)

Here are the options listed in UBS Text Project.

  1. MT ‒ "as bulls, our lips," פרים שׂפתינו
  2. LXX ‒ "the fruit of our lips," פרי משׂפתינו
  3. REB ‒ "bulls from their pens," פרים משׂפתינו

The Jewish Publication Society of America translation, 1999, p. 1165, in a footnote admits this line of poetry is "uncertain."

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

entries.title: Hosea 14:3 "Assyria will not save us"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:3 "Assyria will not save us" In this verse there are allusions to political alliances and the things that human leaders tend to trust:

  1. foreign alliances (Assyria's treaties, i.e. Hosea 5:13)
  2. military power (Egyptian horses, cf. Ps. 20:7; 33:17; Isa. 2:7; 30:16; 31:1)
  3. idols ("work of our hands," i.e. Canaanite fertility gods)

▣ "To the work of our hands" Hosea ridicules idolatry in Hos. 4:12; 14:3; Isaiah in Isa. 2:18,20; 17:7-9; 31:7; and Jeremiah in Jer. 10:3-5,8-9,14-15. This attitude reflects Exod. 20:4-5; 34:17; Lev. 19:4; 26:1; Deut. 4:15-19,25; 5:8.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "For in You the orphan finds mercy" YHWH is again depicted as a merciful parent as in Hosea 11:1-4 (cf. Ps. 68:5; Lam. 5:3). The orphan represents the powerless and vulnerable people of society. YHWH's people should care for these kinds of people (e.g. Exod. 22:21-24; Deut. 10:18-19; 14:29; 16:11-12; 24:17,19; 26:12-13; 27:19).

The VERB "finds mercy" (BDB 933, KB 1216, Pual IMPERFECT) is the same as one of Hosea's children (negated) in Hosea 1:6; 2:4, but mercy is restored in Hosea 2:1,19,23 and here! This is a covenant term like "My people" (cf. Hosea 1:9 vs. 2:1).

entries.title: Hosea 14:4 "I will heal their apostasy"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:4 "I will heal their apostasy" In verses 4-8 YHWH speaks! The VERB (BDB 950, KB 1272) is a Qal IMPERFECT. Healing is an OT imagery for forgiveness (cf. Hosea 5:13; 6:1; 7:1; 11:3; Ps. 103:3; Isa. 57:18; Jer. 3:22).

The term "apostasy" (BDB 1000) is literally "turning back" (cf. Hosea 11:7). It is used in Jeremiah for turning away from YHWH (cf. Jer. 2:19; 3:22; 5:6; 8:5; 14:7; Judah is called faithless in Hosea 3:6,8,11,14; also notice 7:24). If Israel "turns back" (i.e. repents) from sin (cf. Hosea 14:1) YHWH will "heal their turning back" (i.e. apostasy) tendencies! His anger has "turned away from them" (cf. Deut. 30:1-10). Notice the series of sound word plays on shub (BDB 996; see note below).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (aphistēmi)

▣ "I will love them freely" This VERB (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal IMPERFECT) is parallel to "heal" in line 1. Grace (YHWH's unchanging character, cf. Mal. 3:6), not merit (humans ever-changing heart and motives), is the key to the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36; Eph. 2:8-9,10).

However, an initial and ongoing response is demanded, not only repentance and faith (cf. Deut. 30; Mark 1:15; Acts 2:21), but also obedience and perseverance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "My anger has turned away from them" The term "anger" (BDB 60) is from the Hebrew root "nose" or "face." Anger can be seen in a red face and hard breathing. Here, it is an anthropomorphism for YHWH's deep feelings.

There is a play on the word "turn back" or "return" (BDB 996) in this context:

  1. return, Hosea 14:1
  2. return to, Hosea 14:2
  3. turn away, Hosea 14:4
  4. also in Hosea 14:7

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Hosea 14:5 "the dew"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:5 "the dew" Dew (literal here, not like Hosea 6:4; 13:3) is the only source of moisture in Israel between the two rainy periods and is crucial for crops to mature. Verses 5-7 describe the agricultural signs of YHWH's blessings (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27-28).

There is a series of JUSSIVES in Hosea 14:5-6:

  1. "blossom," Hosea 14:5 ‒ BDB 827, KB 965, Qal IMPERFECT ‒ JUSSIVE in meaning
  2. "will stake its roots," Hosea 14:5 (but in this context of positive promises, "will take root") ‒ BDB 645, KB 697, Qal JUSSIVE
  3. "sprout" (lit. "go"), Hosea 14:6 ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT ‒ JUSSIVE in meaning
  4. "will be" ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal JUSSIVE

▣ "Lebanon" This is the nation north of Israel called Phoenicia, whose capital is Tyre. It was famous for its large cypress trees. In this context

  1. trees, Hosea 14:5 (parallel to city)
  2. trees, Hosea 14:6 (parallel to olive trees)
  3. wine, Hosea 14:7 (parallel to vine)

In context, this may be a veiled reference to Ba'al (as 14:2d), who Jezebel from Tyre, brought into Israel. The fertility of Lebanon was from YHWH, not Ba'al (cf. Hosea 14:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

entries.title: Hosea 14:6-7 "olive tree. . .grain. . .vine"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:6-7 "olive tree. . .grain. . .vine" The three main crops of Palestine are olive oil, grains, and grapes. YHWH gave them this fertile land (e.g. Deut. 8:7-9; 11:9-12). These were from YHWH, not Ba'al! The restoration of God's people to the land flowing with milk and honey is described as agricultural abundance (cf. Amos 9:13-15), but in reality it is the intimacy of the personal relationship with the Covenant God that is the greatest joy of a restored and renewed people/family!

entries.title: Hosea 14:7 "Those who live in his shadow"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:7 "Those who live in his shadow" The VERB (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT) means to sit or to dwell. This is imagery for

  1. YHWH as a mother bird who protects her young under her wings (cf. Ps. 17:8; 36:7; 57:1; 63:7; Matt. 23:27)
  2. because of the agricultural context of Hosea 14:5-7 and 8, this probably refers to God as a provider of a fruitful symbolic tree (cf. Hosea 14:8; Ezek. 17:22-24)

It is YHWH, not Ba'al, who is the source of fertility and stability (cf. Hosea 14:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE

entries.title: Hosea 14:8 "what more have I to do with idols"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:8 "what more have I to do with idols" This is a Hebrew idiom of rejection (e.g. Jdgs. 11:12; 2 Sam. 16:10; 19:22; 1 Kgs. 17:18; 2 Kgs. 3:13; 2 Chr. 35:21; John 2:4).

▣ "It is I who answer" Idols cannot answer, but YHWH can. This same VERB (BDB 772, KB 851) is used repeatedly in Hosea 2:21-22, which sets the stage for the great promise of Hosea 2:23!

▣ "and look after you" This VERB (BDB 1003 II, KB 1449, Qal IMPERFECT) has the connotation of "regard with watchful care," (root "to bend down to look at").

This same VERB is used in Hosea 13:7 with the connotation of "lie in wait to ambush" (cf. Jer. 5:26). Context is determinative!

The God of Israel is alive and attentive, while the gods of Canaan are lifeless idols of wood and metal who cannot see, hear, speak, move, or help!

▣ "I am like a luxuriant cypress" This is the only place in the OT that God is described as a tree.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE

▣ "From Me comes your fruit" YHWH, not Ba'al, is the source of blessing. What a tragedy when God's people do not know this truth.

entries.title: Hosea 14:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:9 This is a wisdom proverb much like the book of Revelation, "Let him who has an ear hear." The VERBS "understand" (BDB 106, KB 619) and "discern" (BDB 106, KB 122) are both JUSSIVES (the second in meaning, but not form). The words of Hosea must be read more than once and enacted!

▣ "Whoever" This closing wisdom saying focuses on an individual (not corporate) response to Hosea's teaching. The nation was unable to repent, but individuals can respond to God's love appropriately! Choice is an individual covenantal concept (cf. Ezek. 18; 33). We are responsible individually because we must respond to God individually (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT).

Notice the two admonitions related to wisdom.

  1. let him understand these things ‒ BDB 106, KB 122, Qal JUSSIVE
  2. let him know then ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

▣ "the ways. . .walk. . .stumble" Here are three terms that describe the life of faith in images of physical walking (e.g. Prov. 23:19). This reflects OT Wisdom Literature's "the two ways": choose God, walk in Him and live or choose sin and walk in it (cf. Deut. 30:15-20; Rom. 8:4-5). The early church was originally called "the Way" in Acts. Biblical faith is a lifestyle. Eternal life has observable characteristics.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "right. . .righteous" The Hebrew root is a "straight edge" (i.e. measuring river reed). Today we would say a "ruler." Therefore, all Hebrew words for "sin" refer to a deviation from this standard. The standard is God Himself!

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS FOR CHAPTERS 13 AND 14

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Was Hosea against the concept of monarchy?
  2. Why does Paul quote Hosea 13:14 in 1 Cor. 15?
  3. Describe the literary metaphors used in Hosea 14:9.
  4. What two metaphors does Hosea use to describe God?
  5. What is the central theme of the book?
